question: A PO line has portions for two Jobs and general stock. Explain allocation, Pending Receival, partial receipt and on-hand Inventory, and when reservations exist. Do not make changes.
message:
A PO line can allocate portions to two Jobs, with the remainder for general stock. Allocation is an incoming intent, not on-hand stock or an existing on-hand reservation. After the PO is issued and its permanent PDF generated, Pending Receivals must be created explicitly; they preserve the allocation context but do not add stock.

A partial receipt puts only the quantity actually received into on-hand Inventory; the balance remains pending. Received Job-allocated units become reserved for their respective Jobs, while received general-stock units remain general stock. Reservations can also be made later against existing general-stock lots. A pending allocation alone does not establish supplier arrival or Job readiness.

No changes were made.
